blindSummary: This country carries severe risk for trans visitors. There is no legal gender recognition and no visible community.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): this country has criminalised same-sex conduct since the historic era; a 2014 amendment introduced 'aggravated homosexuality' (life imprisonment) under the then ruler, who publicly threatened to 'decapitate' gay people. A new criminal code (March 2025) removes 'aggravated homosexuality' but sets a minimum of five years for 'unnatural offences' (defined as 'any homosexual act') and three years for 'gross indecency', with no maximum - so any same-sex act could in theory draw life. The current government has not typically enforced.

International democracy-monitoring organisation's 2024 global-freedoms assessment of this country: rated 50/100; freedoms improved under the post-authoritarian government after 22 years of the prior ruler's rule, but LGBT+ people face severe discrimination among ongoing concerns.

A foreign home ministry's country-of-origin information note (v3.0, Feb 2023) on sexual orientation and gender identity or expression in this country: assessment of risk, protection, internal relocation and certification for LGBT+ asylum claims, with detailed country information on law and treatment.

International human-rights organisation's report (Sept 2015) on the climate of fear under the prior regime: arbitrary arrests, torture and killings - includes the context of anti-gay rhetoric and threats against LGBT people.

A foreign government's 2020 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised (up to life imprisonment under the 2013 amendment); documents arrests and societal discrimination.

A foreign government's 2021 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - continued criminalisation, no prosecutions reported, significant societal stigma and police harassment of LGBT persons.
blindTangential: The criminal code criminalises same-sex conduct; a 2014 amendment added an "aggravated homosexuality" offence (life imprisonment for "serial offenders"), and in 2024 the national assembly raised the minimum sentence for homosexual acts to 5 years — the trajectory is towards harsher penalties, not reform. Under the prior regime, LGBTI people faced documented persecution (including the then head of state's infamous public threats to kill gay people); the successor era has seen some improvement in general freedoms but no decriminalisation and continued severe discrimination (per an international democracy monitor). Same-sex criminalisation is the vehicle; trans people are captured via birth-sex status and indecency provisions.
